text: Survey of 12,000 under-40 office workers showed an 11-point blood pressure drop, only alongside salt cuts; daily walks lower pressure.
Coffee improves memory, tested only in university students after a sleepless night, a 2 percent gain on one word test.
Working from home raises productivity, per three start-up software teams, self-rated; the gain vanished after six months.
A new bridge cut bus commutes by about twenty minutes, against a year of major roadworks.
Vitamin D prevents colds, but a single supplement-maker-funded trial in winter, only in under-fives.
A reading app helped English-learning children read, compared with no teaching, but the gains faded by next school year.
Pesticides harm bumblebees: one season in two English counties left colonies with a quarter fewer queens.
A four-day week reduces burnout, per an Icelandic public-sector trial with unchanged pay; sick days didn't change.
